visual_system.palette: Neutral whites, slate equipment, natural copper and wood. Keep real blue equipment and outdoor greens; do not tint them to the brand.
visual_system.light: Prefer readable, evenly lit subjects. Keep genuine work lighting where the task remains clear.
visual_system.tone: Real projects, understandable equipment and approachable people. Friendly work portraits are useful here, despite the skill's stock-photo rule against eye contact.
visual_system.composition: Rank the clearest service view first. Add a useful detail or work view, rather than three nearly identical frames. Favor finished residential fixtures where available.
visual_system.texture: Keep the existing clean JPEG copies. Add no grain, filters or simulated detail.
visual_system.treatment: No crop or color grade applied. Crop notes and focal points guide a later website placement; they are not permission to remove equipment or alter the work.
visual_system.selection_scope: Up to three distinct, useful options per reviewed category. These are ranked alternatives, not three mandatory slots on the website. Uncertain classifications stay excluded.

general-plumbing/piping-and-repiping.cut_reason: The shortlist balances a tidy manifold, a readable wall rough-in and an outdoor pipe route. Other frames repeat these views, obscure connections with framing, or devote more space to soil and loose materials.

general-plumbing/gas-line-repair-and-ins.cut_reason: ID 87's steep overhead angle hides more of the assembly. ID 89 is a detail alternative to 88, not a separate project.

general-plumbing/toilet-repair-and-insta.cut_reason: These show the finished fixture, its connection hardware and room context. Other room views repeat the composition; ID 183 has worn cistern surfaces and little visual context, while ID 128 gives more space to soil than to the toilet connection.

general-plumbing/faucets-fixtures-and-si.cut_reason: The first two lead with finished home fixtures. ID 66 adds a clean utility/commercial sink alternative. Other images duplicate the bathroom view or include more empty wall, storage bins or cropped fixtures.

general-plumbing/showers-and-tubs.cut_reason: Keep the fitting detail, the finished-room overview and the clearer construction-stage tub. Other construction frames contain more wrapping and debris; other finished views repeat this bathroom. These are not a verified before-and-after pair.

general-plumbing/water-filtration-system.cut_reason: Use a complete treatment layout, a tighter filter/UV view and a person with the equipment. Other frames repeat these installations, crop the worker or tank bottoms, or mix treatment vessels with unrelated heating equipment.

water-heaters/system-overview.cut_reason: These keep a storage tank and its connections readable, with equipment-only and human views. Crawlspace alternatives have more overhead ducting, floor membrane and scattered tools. Keep these as general hot-water plant context, not evidence of a specific heater subtype.

drain-and-sewer/sewer-line-repair-and-re.cut_reason: The set gives a clear replacement connection, a cleanout connection and people with removed pipe. IDs 30 and 31 have lower pipe/soil contrast; ID 41 adds clutter to the same connection as 42; ID 57 obscures pipe sections under a deck.

drain-and-sewer/system-overview.cut_reason: The shortlisted views explain wall routing, mixed supply/waste routing and a floor flange connection. Other rough-in frames repeat these subjects or have more tilted framing, overexposure, bare soil or obstructed branches.

water-filtration/uv-treatment.cut_reason: The UV chamber stays visible in a dedicated filter assembly, a full treatment layout and a closer connection view. Other frames repeat the equipment or introduce cropped people, stronger glare and more unused wall.

water-filtration/system-overview.cut_reason: These show readable treatment layouts in neutral surroundings. Other views repeat the installations, crop important vessels or place filtration beside a crowded heating plant.

heating-and-cooling/heating.cut_reason: ID 133 shows the same unit-heater composition at 1280 × 960. Keep ID 149's 1600 × 1200 version rather than filling the shortlist with a redundant image.

boilers/hydronic-heating.cut_reason: These show the plant, circulation pumps and a recognizable radiator. ID 14 contains a towel radiator, but the sink dominates the frame; keep it as a plumbing alternative. ID 86 has a loose display and cable on the floor, but the radiator and pipe connections remain the clear subject. Other frames repeat the plant or add clutter and harsh light.

boilers/system-overview.cut_reason: ID 136 repeats 159's boiler/burner composition at lower resolution. ID 4 repeats 3's work scene. Keep two distinct options rather than three redundant views.

about/on-the-job.cut_reason: These give a clear smiling work portrait, a person with a complete treatment system and a focused tool-use view. Other frames hide faces, add foreground clutter, use harsher light or repeat these views. IDs 107 and 105 are portrait/action alternatives from the same setting; avoid placing them beside each other.
